thread.title: Tech And Semiconductor Stocks: Sell The Rhetoric And Buy The Fear

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Tech And Semiconductor Stocks: Sell The Rhetoric And Buy The Fear
text:
Shutterstock photo Whether you believe in “buy low to sell high” or “buy high to sell higher,” the punishment suffered in semiconductor stocks on Monday has just created a strong buying opportunity for investors who can stomach the volatility.
A report by the Wall Street Journal suggesting that the U.S. is planning even stricter trade measures on China sent names like Nvidia ( NVDA ), Intel ( INTC ), Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) and Micron ( MU ) tumbling on Monday. The latter lost as much as 8% at its low, resulting in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index losing 3% Monday.
Citing people familiar with the matter, the WSJ said that the Treasury Department is crafting rules that will restrict any Chinese firm with a stake of 25% or more from acquiring any U.S.-based company deemed by the Federal government as having “industrially significant technology.” The terms and length of the restriction are still being sorted through. And we won’t know what they are until an official announcement is made at the end of this week.
"The president has made clear his desire to protect American technology," said Wilbur Ross, Commerce Secretary, according to the Journal on Sunday. "All possibilities that would better protect American technology, including potential changes to export controls, are under review."
That’s all well and good, but there’s nothing new here. Trade tensions between the two countries have been escalating to the point where such a measure — assuming the WSJ is correct — became predictable. Not to mention, President Trump campaigned on this exact premise, promising to protect intellectual property of U.S. companies. So, from my vantage point, the drop in tech stocks, particularly chip companies with tons of momentum, is an overreaction.
Meanwhile, the selling hysteria also reached the FAANGs — referring to Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) where they collectively fell by an average of 3%. Investors who decided to take profits and/or rotated out of chip and techs are ignoring the fact that all of these tech giants still have strong fundamentals. Collectively, they’re projected to grow 2018 earnings by an average of 81% — well above 15% projected growth rate of the S&P 500 index.
All told, despite the so-called “headline risk,” the fact remains that corporate revenue and earnings are on the rise. And when compared to the rest of the S&P 500 Index, tech stocks — despite their consistent stock outperformance — are arguably still the cheapest names on the market by virtue of their projected earnings growth rate.
